title: Camera Topology, Geospatial Model, and Travel-Time Constraints
objective: Model the camera network as a graph with plausible travel-time windows between cameras, and expose the plausibility queries that let the matching and path-reconstruction stages prune candidates cheaply instead of searching all sightings everywhere.
context_for_agent: This is the component that turns an unbounded search ('where else did this car appear?') into a bounded one ('which cameras could it have reached between 10:02 and 10:07?'). Its correctness directly determines both false-positive rate and query cost. Keep it pure and dependency-light — it should be testable with no database and no video.

tasks.name: Topology configuration format
tasks.detail: Define config/topology.yaml with two sections: 'cameras' (list of Camera fields) and 'links' (list of CameraLink fields). Support an optional 'defaults' block specifying a default speed model used to auto-derive travel times for links that omit them. Write a documented example file with at least 5 cameras and a mix of explicit and derived links, including one deliberately one-directional link (e.g. a one-way street).

tasks.name: Topology loader and validator
tasks.detail: Implement load_topology(path) -> Topology. Validation must reject: duplicate camera_ids, links referencing unknown cameras, self-links, links whose max_travel_time_sec <= min_travel_time_sec, and duplicate link definitions for the same ordered pair. Raise TopologyError with a message naming the offending entries. Warn (do not fail) on: cameras with no links at all (isolated nodes), and links whose implied speed exceeds a configurable sanity limit (e.g. distance/min_travel_time > 200 km/h).

tasks.name: Travel-time derivation
tasks.detail: When a link omits explicit times, derive them from the great-circle distance between the two cameras and a configurable speed range (default: min_travel_time from max_speed_kph, max_travel_time from min_speed_kph, plus a configurable additive slack in seconds for stops and signals). Apply a configurable road-winding factor (default 1.3) to convert straight-line distance to estimated road distance. All factors live in config and are documented. Mark derived links with a 'derived: true' flag so the source of every constraint is auditable.

tasks.name: Topology graph structure
tasks.detail: Implement a Topology class holding cameras and links with efficient adjacency lookup. Expand bidirectional links into both directed edges at load time so downstream code always works with directed edges. Provide: get_camera(id), list_cameras(), neighbors(camera_id) -> list[CameraLink], get_link(from_id, to_id) -> CameraLink | None, has_link(from_id, to_id) -> bool.

tasks.name: Plausibility queries
tasks.detail: Implement the core API used by later stages: (a) reachable_from(camera_id, departure_time, max_horizon_sec) -> list[ReachableCamera] where each entry carries the target camera and the absolute arrival TimeWindow; (b) is_transition_plausible(from_camera, to_camera, elapsed_sec) -> PlausibilityResult with fields plausible: bool, reason: str enum ('within_window' | 'too_fast' | 'too_slow' | 'no_link' | 'same_camera'), and margin_sec (how far outside the window, 0 if inside); (c) plausibility_score(from_camera, to_camera, elapsed_sec) -> float in [0,1] returning 1.0 inside the window and decaying smoothly outside it according to a configurable decay function, so scoring is graded rather than binary.

tasks.name: Multi-hop reachability
tasks.detail: Implement reachable_within(camera_id, departure_time, max_horizon_sec, max_hops) using a time-constrained breadth-first/Dijkstra-style search over the directed graph. This supports the case where a target passes through an uncovered area and reappears at a camera two or three hops away. Return, for each reachable camera, the earliest and latest plausible arrival times and the hop count. Guard against exponential blowup with a configurable node-visit cap and cycle handling.

tasks.name: Same-camera handling
tasks.detail: Define and implement explicit semantics for repeat sightings on the same camera (a vehicle circling back, or simply lingering in frame). Provide a configurable min_redetection_gap_sec below which two sightings on the same camera are considered the same pass rather than two separate transits. Document the choice; later stages depend on it.

tasks.name: Coverage analysis utilities
tasks.detail: Implement helpers used by stage 08 and the UI: find_isolated_cameras(), graph_diameter_sec(), and describe_gap(from_camera, to_camera, elapsed_sec) producing a human-readable explanation of why a hop was implausible (e.g. 'no known route between cam_01 and cam_07' or 'arrived 240s faster than the minimum plausible transit of 300s').

tasks.name: Topology persistence sync
tasks.detail: Implement sync_topology_to_db(topology, camera_repo, link_repo) which upserts the file-defined topology into the database, and load_topology_from_db(...) for the runtime path. The YAML file is the authoring format; the database is the runtime source of truth. Syncing must be idempotent and must not delete cameras that still have sightings (raise TopologyError instead, listing them).

tests_substage.description: Topology bugs are silent — they produce plausible-looking but wrong paths. Test the boundaries of every time window explicitly.

cases: valid example topology loads with the expected camera and link counts
duplicate camera_id raises TopologyError naming the id
link referencing an unknown camera raises TopologyError naming both the link and the missing camera
self-link rejected
duplicate link for the same ordered pair rejected
max <= min travel time rejected with both values in the message
isolated camera produces a warning but loads successfully
implausible implied speed produces a warning but loads successfully
bidirectional link expands into exactly two directed edges
one-directional link expands into exactly one directed edge and has_link is False in the reverse direction
empty topology file raises TopologyError
malformed YAML raises TopologyError rather than a raw parser exception
explicit times on a link are preserved and NOT overwritten by derivation
omitted times are derived and the link is flagged derived=true
derived min_travel_time corresponds to the configured max speed and derived max to the min speed
winding factor is applied to the straight-line distance
additive slack is included in the max bound
two cameras at identical coordinates produce a non-zero, finite max_travel_time (guard against divide-by-zero)
elapsed exactly equal to min_travel_time is plausible (boundary, inclusive)
elapsed exactly equal to max_travel_time is plausible (boundary, inclusive)
elapsed one second below min returns too_fast with margin_sec == 1
elapsed one second above max returns too_slow with correct margin_sec
unlinked camera pair returns no_link
same camera returns same_camera
negative elapsed time (out-of-order timestamps) raises or returns implausible — document and test the chosen behavior
returns exactly 1.0 anywhere inside the window
decays monotonically as elapsed moves further outside the window in both directions
never returns a value outside [0,1] for any input including extreme values
returns the configured floor value for an unlinked pair rather than raising
single-hop reachability returns exactly the direct neighbors within the horizon
a neighbor whose min_travel_time exceeds the horizon is excluded
two-hop reachability with max_hops=1 excludes the two-hop camera; with max_hops=2 includes it
arrival windows for a two-hop path correctly compound (min sums with min, max sums with max)
a cycle in the graph terminates without infinite looping
node-visit cap is respected and the result is flagged as truncated
results include hop count for every reachable camera
reachability from an isolated camera returns an empty list
two sightings on one camera within min_redetection_gap_sec are treated as one pass
two sightings just beyond the gap are treated as separate transits
find_isolated_cameras identifies exactly the unlinked cameras
describe_gap produces distinct, human-readable messages for no_link, too_fast, and too_slow cases

property_based_tests: For randomly generated topologies: every camera returned by reachable_from is also reported as a neighbor by has_link when hop count is 1.
plausibility_score is always in [0,1] for arbitrary elapsed values including negatives, zero, and very large values.
Expanding bidirectional links twice (idempotency check) does not create duplicate edges.

cases: sync_topology_to_db inserts all cameras and links into a real database
running sync twice is idempotent — no duplicates, no errors
modifying a link in YAML and re-syncing updates the existing row rather than inserting a new one
removing a camera that has sightings raises TopologyError listing that camera
removing a camera with no sightings succeeds
load_topology_from_db reproduces a Topology equal to the one loaded from the YAML file

exit_criteria: The example topology file loads, validates, and syncs to the database cleanly
Every plausibility boundary is covered by an explicit test at the exact boundary value
Multi-hop reachability terminates on cyclic graphs and respects its visit cap
Every derived travel time is traceable to its inputs via the derived flag and documented factors
The module has no database or filesystem dependency in its core query path (pure in-memory graph)
deliverables: docs/TOPOLOGY.md explaining the authoring format and the derivation model
